feedback_text: The professor explains transformer self-attention and tokenization with awesome visual animations and live coding notebooks!
The midterm grading rubric was completely arbitrary and unfair; marks were deducted without a single comment explaining why.
Assigning three heavy deep learning coding projects and a research paper critique in the same week is overwhelming and causes severe anxiety.
The instructor jumps between advanced Fourier transform proofs and code snippets without explaining how they connect, leaving us very confused.
Morning lectures consist entirely of reading verbatim from dense PowerPoint slides in a monotone voice for two straight hours.
Thank you so much to the teaching assistants for staying late during office hours to help me debug my word embedding pipeline!
Half the computers in the database lab crash during SQL query indexing and the local lab server disconnects before every deadline.
It was a really good concept and interesting topic, but the two-hour afternoon lecture felt too long and slow.
The syllabus is brilliantly modernized with state-of-the-art architectures like BERT, GPT, and practical deployment pipelines.
Making the closed-book final exam worth seventy percent of the total grade creates unbearable exam pressure and sleepless nights.
My questions on the course discussion forum have gone completely unanswered for three weeks despite multiple polite reminders.
The syllabus structure is chaotic; advanced probability distributions are taught before the prerequisite calculus foundations are covered.
The bi-weekly assignment schedule was thoughtfully paced and the flexible grace days helped me produce my best engineering work.
The new cloud GPU notebooks and pre-configured Docker containers worked flawlessly and made training neural models a breeze!
The exam problem statements were worded so vaguely that nobody in the hall knew whether to write pseudocode, Python code, or a proof.
The lab manual instructions were written for an older software version, so none of the menu commands match our current lab PCs.
I am deeply grateful to the professor for recording supplemental walkthrough videos and adapting the lecture pace after mid-semester feedback.
Most of the course content simply repeats introductory programming definitions for six weeks, making the syllabus redundant and boring.
Surprise pop quizzes with negative marking keep everyone terrified and anxious throughout the entire semester.
Releasing a massive programming assignment on Friday night and making it due Monday morning is unreasonable and frustrating!
Office hours were super collaborative and helpful; walking through my architecture diagrams with the TA solved all my conceptual doubts.
During practical lab exams, the slow machines freeze for ten minutes at a time, making us panic about losing our code before time runs out.
Different teaching assistants give completely contradictory advice on how to format the final project report, leaving our team confused.
The open-book analytical exams tested genuine conceptual mastery rather than rote memorization—a breath of fresh air!
The instructor rushes through fifty slides in forty minutes and refuses to slow down despite repeated requests from students.
Heartfelt thanks to the teaching team for fostering such a welcoming, respectful, and motivating classroom environment this term.
We are expected to train deep neural networks, yet the department lab machines do not even have the required GPU drivers installed.
The relentless pace of weekly lab submissions leaves zero time to sleep or prepare for other core departmental subjects.
Visualizing mathematical derivations step by step on the board made complex optimization algorithms click immediately.
Two students with nearly identical project implementations received wildly different grades due to inconsistent TA evaluation.
The prescribed textbook is dry, archaic, and completely disconnected from modern data science and engineering applications.
Thank you for extending the capstone project deadline by forty-eight hours when our batch had three midterm exams scheduled.
I cannot figure out how the lab experiments relate to the theoretical lectures because the two tracks are completely out of sync.
Big thanks to the lab technicians for setting up the remote JupyterHub server so we could run experiments from our hostel rooms.
Penalizing twenty percent of the project grade for a minor formatting typo while ignoring the working algorithm is demoralizing.
Learning both classical TF-IDF statistical models and modern neural architectures gave me a complete, satisfying grasp of NLP.
